prd.text:
---
version: 6
date: 2026-10-11
---

# Replace custom onboarding persistence with an AsyncStorage MVP

## Problem

Custom native onboarding persistence prevents the requested simple Expo Go workflow and adds unnecessary build and storage complexity. Replace it entirely so each launch briefly shows Splash, then routes by one completion flag and the existing verified session. This is a new change replacing the native/preview architecture; PRDs v1–v5 remain intact, including the unused v5 draft.

Profile: standard. Startup navigation and authentication boundaries affect every launch; small source changes do not make this low risk.

## Solution

Use the existing AsyncStorage dependency on every supported platform with exactly one onboarding key, `@leafcheck_onboarding_complete`. Store a JSON boolean as a string (`true` or `false`); missing or false means incomplete. Keep existing slide UI and durable completion/retry handling, simplify the marker contract, and remove custom native capability selection entirely. After a brief splash and resolved checks, incomplete onboarding wins over any restored session; otherwise signed-out users see Login and verified authenticated users see Dashboard.

The brief's “JWT in expo-secure-store” means the existing persisted refresh credential used to restore a valid session. Access JWTs remain in memory, as required by AGENTS.md; credential presence alone never proves authentication. Existing server refresh and profile validation remain the authority. No backend or database changes are needed.

## Scope

| This PRD covers | This PRD does NOT cover |
| --- | --- |
| Delete custom module folder, native adapter and native-contract test | New native modules, development-build requirements or dependencies |
| One plain AsyncStorage boolean flag across native and web | SecureStore onboarding persistence or migration of old markers |
| Root startup guards, entry redirect and brief splash on all cold launches | Visual redesign, new slides or changes to API authorization |
| Direct Dashboard startup after verified authentication, including pending garden setup | Deleting garden data, credential changes or removing explicit garden setup functionality |
| Relevant regression tests and current developer/manual guidance | Backend, firmware, database migrations, publishing or git commits |

## Requirements

### R-01 — Remove custom native onboarding persistence

- **S-01:** `frontend/modules/install-onboarding/`, `frontend/services/install-onboarding-storage.native.ts` and `frontend/tests/install-onboarding-native-contract.test.ts` no longer exist. Active onboarding code contains no InstallOnboarding native module loader, runtime capability selection or fallback split.
- **S-02:** Expo Go boots and completes onboarding without a custom native build; standalone/development/web resolve the same standard storage contract. Current README and manual onboarding instructions no longer require the deleted module. Historical PRDs/evidence remain preserved.

### R-02 — Persist one boolean in AsyncStorage

- **S-03:** Given an absent key or stored `false`, startup treats onboarding as incomplete. Stored `true` means complete; both are string-serialized JSON booleans, never the old versioned object.
- **S-04:** Finishing the final slide writes `true` under exactly `@leafcheck_onboarding_complete`; a new store or app reload skips slides. No onboarding read/write touches SecureStore or any legacy onboarding key.
- **S-05:** Malformed/nonboolean records or rejected reads produce recoverable storage feedback after Splash, without granting completion or clearing unrelated data. A failed final write retains the slide and allows retry; completion occurs only after successful persistence. Concurrent completion calls cannot double-submit.
- **S-06:** Login, logout, account changes and guest entry do not reset the completion flag or write credentials/garden data to it. Existing marker locations are ignored: the new missing key deliberately shows onboarding once again.

### R-03 — Apply the strict startup destinations

- **S-07:** Given missing/false onboarding and either anonymous or authenticated session state, after Splash show Onboarding and prevent Login/Dashboard deep links from bypassing it. Completing onboarding proceeds according to the resolved session.
- **S-08:** Given `true` and no stored native refresh credential, show Login after Splash. An expired/rejected credential follows the existing verified signed-out result and also shows Login; never infer authentication from a nonempty token string.
- **S-09:** Given `true` and a successfully restored authenticated session, show Dashboard (`/(tabs)`) after Splash, even when account-local garden setup is pending. Remove automatic pending-setup startup redirects in both root guards and entry routing while retaining explicit setup navigation and account data isolation.
- **S-10:** Existing explicit guest entry, login/register, logout and protected account routes retain their access controls after startup. Session restoration failures retain existing recovery; network/storage errors never open protected Dashboard as authenticated. Onboarding I/O failure cannot alter credentials.

### R-04 — Show a brief Splash during startup checks

- **S-11:** Every cold launch renders the existing branded Splash while completion and session checks run, including returning authenticated/signed-out users. Retain a brief two-second minimum display using the existing timing convention; do not release a completed-onboarding launch until session restoration resolves.
- **S-12:** Slow checks retain Splash until the relevant result is ready. Missing/false flag may reveal slides after its read and splash timer even if auth restoration is still pending; final routing waits for session resolution. Timer cleanup prevents updates after unmount, and repeated provider renders do not restart the minimum indefinitely. Failures end in recoverable feedback rather than an indefinite splash.

### R-05 — Verify the MVP and update evidence

- **S-13:** Run `npm test` in both workspaces after implementation (equivalent repository command: `npm test --workspaces`) and `npm run typecheck --workspace=frontend`; all pass. Tests exercise the boolean storage contract, all three destinations, returning-user splash and failure/retry behavior. Remove superseded native-contract tests and update obsolete startup expectations rather than keeping contradictory assertions.
- **S-14:** On real Expo Go, observe missing/false → Onboarding, true/no credential → Login, true/verified session → Dashboard, plus reload persistence and brief Splash each time. Record platform/runtime and results; automated Node/component tests alone cannot claim this device verification passed.

## Architecture

### Structure

```text
frontend/
  modules/install-onboarding/                        delete entire folder
  services/install-onboarding-storage.native.ts       delete
  services/install-onboarding-storage.ts              shared AsyncStorage adapter
  services/install-onboarding-store.ts                boolean parser and startup phase logic
  context/install-onboarding.tsx                      keep small shared provider
  app/_layout.tsx                                    startup gating and Dashboard guards
  app/index.tsx                                      matching entry destinations
  app/splash.tsx                                     brief splash lifecycle
  tests/install-onboarding-native-contract.test.ts    delete
  tests/install-onboarding-*.test.ts                  updated storage/routing coverage
  tests/startup-*.ts and relevant routing tests        update affected expectations
  README.md and tests/INSTALL_ONBOARDING_MANUAL_CHECKS.md update
```

### Components and data flow

A shared storage adapter calls AsyncStorage `getItem`/`setItem` for one fixed key. The existing injectable intro store validates boolean strings, coalesces in-flight operations and owns completion/read/write failure state. Preserve its placement outside account-keyed providers so authentication changes cannot reset slides. Root startup routing combines splash readiness, intro completion and the existing auth coordinator; it must not rebuild credential validation inside onboarding code.

Cold launch → show Splash and read flag/restore session in parallel → resolve brief splash timer → incomplete flag: slides; completed flag: wait for verified session → Login or Dashboard. Successful slide completion → persist true → wait for auth if needed → Login or Dashboard. Garden-local hydration and its existing recoverable failures still protect rendering; pending garden setup no longer selects the startup destination. Keep explicit setup screens available through existing actions.

### Load-bearing paths, coverage and blast radius

`_layout.tsx`, `index.tsx`, `splash.tsx`, the intro store/provider and session restoration are load-bearing. Existing onboarding storage/routing/integration, startup characterization, session, garden navigation and spaces-flow tests protect their behavior. The frontend native-contract test currently encodes the architecture being removed and must be replaced by meaningful shared-adapter coverage. No app config module reference was found; implementation must also search active configuration, lockfile and documentation for remaining native-module references.

Rollback restores the prior tracked files and route rules without deleting the new flag, credentials or garden data. The prior custom native design would again require its native build and ignore the new AsyncStorage flag. No migration or write to old stores is proposed; users with only old records see onboarding once under the new key.

## Success Criteria

| Criterion | How to verify |
| --- | --- |
| Shared single-key persistence and no custom module | Adapter tests, deleted-path checks and active-reference search |
| All three startup destinations and minimum splash | Store/component integration tests, including pending garden setup |
| Failure handling and secure auth preserved | Read/write rejection, malformed boolean, session and protected-route regressions |
| Compiles and existing tests pass | `npm run typecheck --workspace=frontend`; `npm test --workspaces` |
| Actual Expo Go operation | Real-device matrix in S-14, recorded honestly if unavailable |

Baseline on 2026-10-11: `npm test --workspaces` passed 337 frontend tests and 94 backend tests, with zero failures; frontend TypeScript passed. Logs are `/tmp/leafcheck-plan-baseline.log` and `/tmp/leafcheck-plan-typecheck.log` (temporary local files). Expo Go device verification has not been performed. Post-implementation checks remain required; this planning invocation does not implement the change.

## Visual Direction

Preserve the existing calm botanical screens, light splash background, logo, typography and palette. Keep current onboarding slide layout and accessible recovery/actions. No artwork, new animation, spacing redesign or native-build explanation in product UI. A visual preference question was offered; preserving existing visuals is the default unless the user supplies a change.

## Security & Trust Boundaries

The flag is untrusted, nonsecret UX state, parsed strictly as a boolean; it never authorizes API access. AsyncStorage must never hold refresh credentials or access JWTs. Native refresh credentials retain existing SecureStore settings, web refresh uses existing HttpOnly cookies, and access JWTs stay in memory. Existing backend refresh/profile checks validate authentication; sanitized failures remain user-visible without raw token values or storage diagnostics.

## Dependencies & Risks

Installed AsyncStorage is 2.2.0; registry `npm view` on 2026-10-11 returned 3.1.1. Keep the existing version: [Expo documentation](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/async-storage/) recommends 2.2.0 and confirms inclusion in Expo Go. Installed dependency types confirm `getItem(key): Promise<string | null>` and `setItem(key, value): Promise<void>`, so the boolean must be serialized. SecureStore registry version is 57.0.4; no dependency upgrades are requested.

AsyncStorage avoids Keychain syncing for this marker, but does not promise exclusion from ordinary app backup/restore. Prior native backup-exclusion guarantees are explicitly removed by this MVP request. Expo Go storage clearing is distinct from reinstalling a standalone app; manual checks should state how storage was cleared. A missing new key intentionally replays intro despite any legacy record. Removing forced garden setup changes startup behavior; Dashboard must handle existing pending/empty garden data without fabricating completion.

## Out of Scope

Custom native persistence, old-record migration or cleanup, backup-exclusion/device-transfer guarantees, storing access JWTs in SecureStore, new auth logic, onboarding redesign, dependency upgrades, backend/database/firmware changes, pushing, publishing, merging and local commits. No delivery time budget was supplied. The user invoked planning; implementation and post-change verification follow through pincer-narrow/pincer-code.

## Authorization and Original Brief

The current user explicitly requests deletion of the entire custom module, the native adapter and native-contract test; reverting native-dependent layout changes; and implementing the strict three-state AsyncStorage MVP. This authorizes the architecture and scope above without another approval for the same decisions. Auth handling interprets “valid JWT exists” through existing verified restoration, consistent with the supplied AGENTS.md access-token rule. AGENTS.md prohibits commits unless explicitly requested (except evaluation); therefore this planning draft is saved without a git commit despite the generic skill commit step.

Original brief:

> TASK: Revert custom native module. Implement simple AsyncStorage MVP solution.
>
> The previous solution over-engineered the onboarding persistence using a custom native module, which broke Expo Go compatibility. We are reverting this entirely for a simple, scalable MVP.
>
> DELETE frontend/modules/install-onboarding/ (entire folder), frontend/services/install-onboarding-storage.native.ts, and frontend/tests/install-onboarding-native-contract.test.ts. REVERT any changes to frontend/app/_layout.tsx that rely on this native module. IMPLEMENT using standard @react-native-async-storage/async-storage.
>
> Use one key: @leafcheck_onboarding_complete (boolean). Null or false → Onboarding. True AND no JWT in expo-secure-store → Login. True AND valid JWT → Dashboard. Splash always shows briefly while checks run. Do NOT use expo-secure-store for onboarding; plain AsyncStorage prevents iCloud Keychain syncing across devices.
>
> Strict TypeScript/AGENTS.md apply. Must work in Expo Go without a custom native build. Run npm test after implementing.

## Objective
Replace native/preview onboarding persistence with one shared AsyncStorage boolean contract, protected by focused behavior tests.

## Context
Implements: R-01, R-02
Owns S-01, storage/runtime contract portion of S-02, S-03–S-06; T-21 owns their UI integration and T-22 owns current guidance and real-device review.
Read frontend/services/install-onboarding-storage.ts, its native adapter, install-onboarding-store.ts, context/install-onboarding.tsx and tests/install-onboarding-storage.test.ts before editing. The provider currently sits outside account-keyed providers; keep this lifetime. The installed AsyncStorage dependency already supplies native/web storage.

## Requirements
- Delete the entire frontend/modules/install-onboarding/ folder, frontend/services/install-onboarding-storage.native.ts and frontend/tests/install-onboarding-native-contract.test.ts. Check active config and lockfile for custom module references; remove only obsolete references.
- Shared install-onboarding-storage.ts uses AsyncStorage only, key @leafcheck_onboarding_complete, with no runtime/environment switch or legacy marker migration.
- Store string-serialized JSON booleans; null/false mean incomplete, true means complete. Reject malformed and nonboolean input with existing sanitized recoverable errors. Never silently rewrite corrupt records or delete unrelated state.
- Preserve read/write coalescing, retry, durable completion before unlocking, and provider independence from account generations. Leave auth credential handling unchanged.
- Update focused storage tests and add tests/install-onboarding-asyncstorage.test.ts using the existing isolated adapter-loading pattern with an injected AsyncStorage implementation. Assert exact keys/values, reload persistence, legacy-key isolation, synchronous/rejected I/O recovery and no SecureStore/native loader use. Test nonboolean rejection and no writes on reads.
- Keep existing UI-compatible state methods until T-21 integrates any splash-phase changes; update affected persistence assertions in integration fixtures without prematurely changing route expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Required native paths are deleted and shared adapter runs without custom native capability.
- [ ] Missing/false/true records produce correct completion decisions; writes persist only true to the exact new key and reload retains it.
- [ ] Malformed records, rejected reads and rejected writes are recoverable, do not unlock completion and do not alter credentials or garden data.
- [ ] Concurrent loads/taps coalesce and completion becomes observable only after successful write.
- [ ] Legacy markers and account/session changes cannot supply or reset the new completion flag.

## Verification
Proves: Real store and injected shared adapter exercise persistence, boolean rejection, retry and durable write ordering; deleted-path assertions prove the static removal contract.
```bash
set -euo pipefail
test ! -e frontend/modules/install-onboarding
test ! -e frontend/services/install-onboarding-storage.native.ts
test ! -e frontend/tests/install-onboarding-native-contract.test.ts
(cd frontend && node --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/install-onboarding-storage.test.ts tests/install-onboarding-asyncstorage.test.ts)
npm run typecheck --workspace=frontend
```

## Constraints
Strict TypeScript without any; no new dependencies, backend/database edits, credential relocation, legacy cleanup, design changes or commits. Historical PRDs and evidence remain intact. Focused tests are required work, not evidence already obtained.

## Objective
Integrate the strict three-state startup routing with a brief branded Splash on every cold launch while preserving verified auth and account isolation.

## Context
Implements: R-02, R-03, R-04
Owns UI preservation/recovery in S-05/S-06 and S-07–S-12.
Read frontend/app/_layout.tsx, app/index.tsx, app/splash.tsx, app/onboarding.tsx, app/setup/_layout.tsx, context/install-onboarding.tsx, context/auth.tsx, services/session.ts and relevant startup/onboarding tests. Existing startup guards and entry redirects force pending authenticated garden setup; both must change together. Auth restoration validates a SecureStore refresh credential with existing server refresh/profile checks.

## Requirements
- Every cold launch shows existing Splash for at least the existing two-second duration while flag/session checks run. Track this per startup, with timer cleanup; rerenders must not restart it indefinitely.
- After flag read and minimum splash, missing/false reveals slides regardless of auth restore outcome; incomplete intro blocks protected/deep-linked Login/Dashboard navigation. Preserve current slide progression when auth changes.
- Completion writes must succeed before routing. For completed intro, wait for restore then show Login when signed out or Dashboard when authenticated, including pending garden setup. Never treat nonempty credentials as a verified session.
- Remove forced setup destination/guard restrictions in root and entry while preserving explicit setup actions/screens, guest entry and protected account routes. Dashboard handles empty/pending garden state without fabricating setup completion.
- Keep Splash until slow relevant checks resolve; after the brief minimum, malformed/failed flag reads expose storage recovery and auth failures expose existing session recovery. Avoid indefinite splash or protected-route flashes.
- Keep onboarding provider outside account-keyed providers; local hydration errors keep their existing retry behavior. Neither storage errors nor auth generations reset the flag or mutate credentials/garden data.
- Update real component/store tests in install-onboarding-routing.test.ts, install-onboarding-integration.test.ts and startup-characterization.test.ts, plus affected helpers/garden-navigation/spaces-flow assertions. Exercise timer scheduling/cleanup, deferred reads/restores/writes, all flag/session combinations, rejected credentials, guest entry and deep-link/back guards. Use existing session tests as preservation evidence; change session logic only if necessary for this authorized behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Null/false plus anonymous/authenticated/restoring/error session shows slides after Splash with no bypass.
- [ ] True plus absent/rejected credential resolves to Login; true plus verified restore resolves to Dashboard even with pending setup.
- [ ] Returning and fresh launches show the same branded two-second minimum Splash; slow checks, cleanup and rerenders behave deterministically.
